newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE COCOA ENDS NEAR UNCHANGED AFTER RALLY FADES.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE COCOA ENDS NEAR UNCHANGED AFTER RALLY FADES.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa drifted down from earlier, currency inspired, highs to end tightly mixed, after arbitrage buying against New York petered out, traders said.
"It's just been drifting off," one trader said. "There was good buying initially on New York," he said.
Sterling's sharp fall against the dollar triggered the rise in morning trade.
Losses in New York, under pressure from a wave of speculative long liquidation, weighed on the London market.
By the close active September was one stg higher at 1,002 stg, compared with a high for the day of 1,017 stg. September volume was 1,461 lots, of the total 4,795.
German cocoa processors have no plans to revise their buying targets for beans and butter, which are 0.15-0.20 marks per kilo below the price range on offer, traders said.

Futures were viewed as too high against the background of fundamentals information while sterling's historic strength versus the mark also choked off demand -- despite the currency's four-pfennig dive on Wednesday.
